text:
Noah Patel: Quick Q - my surrogacy delivery is scheduled during the end-of-quarter performance review week. Need to confirm: can my review be postponed, how does a mid-cycle salary increase interact with parental top-up, and do I need to do anything special for benefits continuity while I'm on leave?

Sofia (People Ops): Congrats Noah! :tada: Short answers: you can postpone the review — managers coordinate with People Ops to reschedule. For salary increases: if the effective date is during leave, comp will still apply but your top-up is calculated based on base pay + effective comp if the increase is approved before payroll cutoff. Please let compensation know ASAP.

Dan (Manager): I'm happy to postpone Noah's review. @people-ops, can you note that we'll reschedule to the quarter after return unless Noah prefers an earlier written-only review?

Noah Patel: Prefer postponement to after return and a written summary in the interim if needed. Also, is there a specific form for comp + top-up coordination?

compensation-bot: Compensation note: To apply a raise effective during leave, submit COMP-REQ form and include approved effective date. Link: https://intranet.redwood.com/comp/raise-request. If approved post-payroll cutoff, raise will be applied retroactively and top-up will be adjusted accordingly.

Sofia (People Ops): For forms: file the parental leave request and check the "compensation overlap" checkbox. We'll coordinate payroll and comp once both requests are in. Payroll cutoff for mid-month increases is typically 10 business days prior to pay date.

payroll-bot: Payroll reminder: to ensure new salary is used for parental top-up calculation, submit comp approval by 2155556700. Otherwise, top-up will be calculated on pre-increase salary and corrected in a retro payroll adjustment.

Noah Patel: Got it. I'll ping comp and submit the leave form today. One more - does taking leave during a performance cycle affect eligibility for bonus/prorated equity refreshes?

Sofia (People Ops): Bonuses: eligibility is handled by compensation policy. Short leaves (within policy) normally do not disqualify you; prorating rules vary. For refresh grants, check the grant docs or ask comp for the specific case. We'll flag your file so comp considers leave timing when assessing PR-related grants.

Dan (Manager): For team coverage, I propose a 10-business-day overlap for handoff and we assign a contractor for 8 weeks. Noah, do you want me to draft the manager handoff message?

Noah Patel: Yes please draft and I'll tweak. Also need IT to create a temporary account for contractor access limited to repo X and runbook Y.

Sofia (People Ops): We'll coordinate contractor laptop and asset transfer. Please confirm contractor start/end dates. IT will limit access as requested. People Ops will also reserve a lactation room post-return and set up phased return paperwork if you want reduced hours.

Dan (Manager): Handoff draft (copy/paste):
```
Hi team,
Noah will be on parental leave START_DATE to END_DATE. During that time, primary contact: Dan (dan@redwood.com). Contractor NAME will cover day-to-day and has access to repo X and runbook Y. Noah will do a 10-business-day overlap before START_DATE for knowledge transfer. For urgent incidents contact on-call. Thanks.
```

payroll-bot: HR ticket opened: HR-PL-2026-478. People Ops will follow up with comp/payroll steps within 2 business days.

Noah Patel: Thank you all 49a. I'll upload expected delivery docs and submit COMP-REQ today. Appreciate the help!
